entry.title: Stop the hurt, then understand the moment
entry.summary: Davies keeps an adult close enough to stop hitting, biting, or pushing. Understanding the feeling goes alongside protecting everyone; repair waits until calm.
entry.cue: There has been physical conflict, or you have noticed situations where it is becoming likely.
detail: Her first response is to stop the harmful action and move children apart when needed. Acknowledging a feeling does not mean allowing the action to continue.

At a calmer time, notice patterns: what was happening, who was nearby, how noisy or crowded it was, and how the adults responded. Davies offers these as clues for adjusting support, not proof of a child’s motive.
After calm, she helps the child check on the other person and models making amends. Laughter does not change the protective limit or prove why the child acted.
